kinds.a: moored houseboat · woonboot · woonschip · schark · float home (hull type)
kinds.d: A hull without its own propulsion and steering, made to stay moored as a dwelling.
t: steel ship hull with built superstructure (schark)

x.a: Srinagar houseboat · Kashmir houseboat · Nageen Lake houseboat
x.d: Stationary wooden houseboat with carved wood panelling moored at the edges of Dal and Nageen lakes, Srinagar; up to three bedrooms plus living room and kitchen.

v.d: Lavish houseboats commissioned by the British to get round the Maharaja's restriction on building houses in the valley.
Built, owned and maintained by Kashmiri Hanji people, now largely let to visitors.

x.dt: size (one to three bedrooms) · carving · mooring (Dal or Nageen Lake)

x.a: Richardson Bay floating home · Waldo Point houseboat · Gates Co-op houseboat
x.d: Self-built or architect-designed home on a reused hull or barge, mostly encased in concrete, docked in the Richardson Bay communities north of Sausalito.

v.d: Reused abandoned boats and material from the decommissioned Marinship shipyards; anchor-outs later moved to approved docks.
245 floating homes on five docks; most hulls encased in concrete.
Built by architect Keith Emons around the bisected carriage of a 1900 Pullman car.
Former steam schooner refitted as a home.
Horned wooden tower with wide-eyed windows.

x.dt: hull (ferry, tug, barge, concrete) · dock (Waldo Point, Gates Co-op, Galilee Harbor) · style (shack, pagoda, Victorian)

x.d: Dutch canal houseboat on a converted inland-vessel or steel hull with a built-on superstructure, holding a registered berth and street address.

v.d: Traditional or historic inland vessel taken out of service and given a stationary living function.
Metal ship or barge hull with a timber, masonry or plastic superstructure; dry-docked every five years.
Steel inland cargo ship converted to a residential houseboat; now the Woonbootmuseum on the Prinsengracht.
Small fully fitted houseboat on an aluminium or plastic float, modelled on land tiny houses.

kinds.a: floating house · float home · woonark · ark · waterwoning · amphibious house
kinds.d: A dwelling on a float or hull moored in a slip, connected to shore utilities, not made to navigate.
t: concrete barge chained to lake bed

x.a: Lake Union houseboat · Portage Bay houseboat · Pacific Northwest float house
x.d: House built on a float and moored to a dock on Lake Union or Portage Bay, descended from loggers' and fishermen's floating shacks.

v.d: One of Seattle's oldest; cottage-style, 2770 Westlake Avenue N, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1982.
Boatworker-built homes with rounded sprung roofs and careful joinery.
Cheap shelter built on discarded cedar logs; many survivors on the water date from this period.
Built on concrete and foam floats rather than logs after the Floating Homes Association secured sewer connections.
Related community: Willamette and Columbia river moorages, Hayden Island the prominent example; largest in the US.
Related community: Canada's first legalised floating home community, on the Fraser River.
Related form: built on concrete barges chained to the lake bottom and docked year-round; no motor, so not a vessel.

x.dt: float (log, concrete, foam) · storeys · moorage slip · lake (Union, Portage Bay, Washington)

x.d: Concrete hull (casco) carrying a timber, masonry or plastic superstructure, moored at a registered berth; the standard modern Dutch floating home.

v.d: 46 households on 30 arks in the Johan van Hasseltkanaal, Amsterdam-Noord; self-built sustainable floating neighbourhood.
32 amphibious and 14 floating houses on the Maas by developer Dura Vermeer with Factor Architecten and Boiten; anchored to posts, rising up to 5.5 m in floods.

x.a: Waterbuurt-West floating house · waterwoning IJburg · Steigereiland floating house
x.d: Purpose-built detached floating house with a timber superstructure over a one-piece cast concrete tub, built at a shipyard, towed across the IJsselmeer and anchored to the lake bed.

v.d: 55 individual floating houses among 158 waterside homes, each with its own jetty; density about 100 homes per hectare.

x.dt: tub (concrete, part-submerged bedrooms) · jetty · floating terrace

brands.d: Amsterdam practice (Marlies Rohmer, Floris Hund) that designed the IJburg Waterbuurt-West floating houses, completed 2011.
Office founded by Koen Olthuis in 2003 as the first practice focused wholly on floating architecture; designs luxury floating houses in IJburg and abroad.
Vancouver-area builder of engineered concrete floats for floating homes, marinas and breakwaters.

traditions.r: Dal and Nageen lakes, Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir
traditions.d: Wooden stationary houseboats with intricately carved panelling, first commissioned by the British and since 1947 built, owned and run by the Hanji lake people.
traditions.tech: timber hull and cabin carpentry with carved wood panelling
traditions.auth: Moored, non-navigating wooden hull; carved interior panelling; berth on Dal or Nageen Lake.

notes: Both old kinds (k10 Houseboat, k11 Floating home) kept; old retail sources replaced by Wikipedia/HistoryLink/architect pages retrieved this session. Navigable craft excluded as vehicles (G1): the Kerala kettuvallam (motorised, oar/punt steered per its Wikipedia page), Australian Murray River pontoon houseboats, Laos slow boats and US lake rental houseboats. Commercial/institutional floating buildings (botels, floating restaurants, student boats, detention boats) dropped under the scope rule. Portland, Ladner and Toronto communities recorded as related versions under the Seattle archetype rather than separate archetypes because no dedicated page was retrieved for them. Dura Vermeer (Maasbommel developer) named in the version note but not registered as a brand because no page about the company itself was retrieved. Tier brands limited to three retrievable floating-home designers/float builders; no SKU lists exist for this market.
